chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Raja, he said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Aban, from Ibn Abbas -- or from Aban ibn Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik -- he said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:
Whoever shows enmity toward Ali has waged war against God, and whoever doubts in Ali is a disbeliever.

key_terms.حارب: Haraba — to wage war, to be at war with; here metaphorical for opposing the divine will
key_terms.كافر: Kafir — disbeliever, one who rejects the truth; here indicating the severity of doubting Ali's station
key_terms.ناصب: Nasaba — to show enmity, hostility; a Nasibi is one who actively opposes Ali and the Ahlulbayt

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about showing enmity toward Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition narrated through two alternative chains reaching companions Ibn Abbas and Anas ibn Malik, the Prophet Muhammad (s) declares that showing enmity toward Imam Ali (AS) is equivalent to waging war against God, and harboring doubt about Ali constitutes disbelief. This was delivered in the context of establishing Ali's divinely-ordained authority, where the early Muslim audience understood nasb (enmity) as the active opposition to Ali's position that the Prophet had repeatedly affirmed.
